title: KneeFS-Net: A Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Knee Osteoarthritis Severity Assessment with Cross-Domain External Validation
abstract: arXiv:2611.19988v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) grading from radiographs using the Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scale requires expertise that may be scarce. We present KneeFS-Net, a lightweight ordinal grader (0.8 million parameters; 0.33 GFLOPs) combining spatial, Fourier and state-space features with landmark-guided attention. On the Osteoarthritis Initiative (OAI) test set, KneeFS-Net achieved a quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) of 0.863, mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.325 and 97.2% within-one-grade accuracy, comparable to models with 9-35-fold more parameters. We evaluated cross-population generalization on two Bangladeshi cohorts, a single-center hospital cohort and a multi-center teleradiology cohort. Without further training or adaptation, the OAI-trained model achieved QWK 0.803, MAE 0.339 and 98.2% within-one-grade accuracy on its hospital cohort, declining to QWK 0.656 and MAE 0.522 on multi-center teleradiology images. Self-supervised pretraining on 6,092

tldr: KneeFS-Net是一种仅含80万参数的轻量级深度学习模型，通过融合空间、傅里叶和状态空间特征进行膝关节X线片KL分级，在OAI数据集上达到QWK 0.863，性能媲美参数量大9-35倍的模型，并在孟加拉国不同人群中展现了跨域泛化能力。
en_tdlr: KneeFS-Net is a lightweight (0.8M-parameter) deep learning model combining spatial, Fourier, and state-space features with landmark-guided attention for knee osteoarthritis KL grading, achieving QWK 0.863 on OAI—comparable to models with 9-35x more parameters—and demonstrating cross-population generalization on Bangladeshi cohorts.
